hits.draft_en:
If Claude Code is part of your daily stack, read the harness engineering paper from Wavestone AI Lab.

They went through the source of 11 coding agents (Codex and Claude Code among them). Every strong one shares the same 7-piece harness. The formula: model + harness = agent.

Each piece, from minimal to maxed out:
- loop: a basic while loop at the low end, fully replayable runs at the top
- LLM layer: anywhere from a single prompt template to 29 provider profiles
- tools: just bash, or 43 typed tools pulled in on demand
- memory: raw chat history at first, persistent notes across sessions later
- safety: from a simple step cap to rules plus a reviewer model plus a sandbox
- orchestration: Aider does without sub-agents, all the others spawn them
- extensions: SKILL.md skills show up in 9 out of 11, MCP in 8

Where to start reading:
- p.4 for the whole 7-piece map
- p.12 for the three loop styles, using Codex and Claude Code as examples
- p.67 for 18 design rules
- p.71 for a 90-line harness that hits all 7 pieces

The model grabs the attention. Whether the AI agent actually gets the job done is down to the harness.

If you can sketch these 7 pieces on a whiteboard, you're who teams hire to build agents.

Full guide to harnesses that survive real workloads below

🚨 If anything you run touches PHP, stop scrolling.

The FBI just issued a warning about 2 critical PHP bugs.

They're being called PHP2Shell.

Here's what you need to know in 60 seconds.

What it is:

→ 2 bugs in the core of PHP itself
→ an attacker can run code on your server
→ no login needed
→ reportedly one single web request is enough

Why it's scary:

PHP powers a huge share of the web.

WordPress.

Laravel apps.

Old client sites nobody has touched in years.

Vendor products that quietly bundle PHP inside.

And Amazon's threat team says it caught someone trying to exploit this 4 days BEFORE it was made public.

What to do right now:

1. Update PHP
Fixed versions: 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35

2. Find every place PHP runs
Prioritize anything facing the internet first

3. Can't patch today?
Take it offline until you can. That's the FBI's advice, not mine.

4. Watch your servers
PHP launching command shells or downloading files is a red flag

5. Found something?
Isolate the system, save your logs, and report it at https://t.co/Ip9MrhmVYe

The builder tip:

If you have a pile of old projects, open Claude Code in each repo and ask:

"Find every place this project uses PHP, list the version, and tell me what needs updating."

The scariest part isn't the bug.

It's the thousands of old sites that will never get patched.

Don't let one of them be yours.

Save this and send it to whoever runs your servers.

The FBI put out a warning on 2 critical flaws in PHP's core. People are calling it PHP2Shell.

- the bugs live in PHP itself, not some plugin
- an attacker can execute code on your server
- no credentials required
- one web request may be all it takes, per reports

Amazon's threat team says it spotted an exploit attempt 4 days before the disclosure went public.

Your checklist:
1. Patch. Safe versions are 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35
2. Map everywhere PHP is running, internet-facing stuff first
3. Can't update today? Pull it offline until you can (the FBI's call, not mine)
4. Monitor your servers. PHP spawning command shells or pulling down files is a warning sign
5. Spotted something? Cut the box off, keep the logs, report it

Quick win for builders: open Claude Code in every old repo in your stack and have it list each spot that relies on PHP, note the version and flag what needs an update.

The bug isn't the scary part. The scary part is the thousands of abandoned sites nobody will ever patch.

Make sure none of them are yours. Save this and forward it to whoever handles your servers.

this is one of the most INSANE open-source AI trading projects on GitHub right now

real trading firms spend millions on analysts, researchers, traders and risk managers

someone built an open-source framework that recreates the entire decision-making process using AI agents that debate each other before making a trade

it's called TradingAgents

here's how it works:

4 AI analysts independently examine fundamentals, technical indicators, financial news and market sentiment

a BULL researcher and a BEAR researcher debate whether the market should go higher or lower

a trader agent turns their arguments into a BUY, SELL or HOLD decision

3 risk perspectives challenge the proposed trade before a portfolio manager makes the final call

here's how to build it yourself for FREE:

step 1 → open Claude Code and ask it to clone https://t.co/eJWTC3a5ul and install the project using Python or Docker

step 2 → configure your AI provider and connect Claude Opus 5.5 for deep reasoning and Sonnet 5.5 for faster research, using the corresponding API credentials

step 3 → launch TradingAgents, select ETH-USD, choose an analysis date and configure how deeply the agents should research the market

step 4 → let the 4 analysts investigate Ethereum using technical indicators, fundamentals, financial news and sentiment data

step 5 → watch the BULL and BEAR researchers challenge each other's conclusions before the trader agent proposes a BUY, SELL or HOLD decision

step 6 → send the proposed trade through the risk management team, where aggressive, neutral and conservative perspectives evaluate the downside before portfolio approval

step 7 → collect the final decisions, plot the signals on an ETH chart and compare them against historical price movements to evaluate the strategy

step 8 → backtest the decisions across multiple market conditions with realistic fees and slippage before even considering real capital

the result: an open-source multi-agent trading research system where AI analysts debate market opportunities, challenge risk and produce structured trading decisions

the framework is free, although AI API usage may cost money, and the terminal in the clip is a visual demonstration rather than live executed trades

this is one of the most INSANE open-source AI trading projects on GitHub right now

real trading firms spend millions on analysts, researchers, traders and risk managers

someone built an open-source framework that recreates the entire decision-making process using AI agents that debate each other before making a trade

it's called TradingAgents

here's how it works:

4 AI analysts independently examine fundamentals, technical indicators, financial news and market sentiment

a BULL researcher and a BEAR researcher debate whether the market should go higher or lower

a trader agent turns their arguments into a BUY, SELL or HOLD decision

3 risk perspectives challenge the proposed trade before a portfolio manager makes the final call

here's how to build it yourself for FREE:

step 1 → open Claude Code and ask it to clone https://t.co/eJWTC3a5ul and install the project using Python or Docker

step 2 → configure your AI provider and connect Claude Opus 5.5 for deep reasoning and Sonnet 5.5 for faster research, using the corresponding API credentials

step 3 → launch TradingAgents, select ETH-USD, choose an analysis date and configure how deeply the agents should research the market

step 4 → let the 4 analysts investigate Ethereum using technical indicators, fundamentals, financial news and sentiment data

step 5 → watch the BULL and BEAR researchers challenge each other's conclusions before the trader agent proposes a BUY, SELL or HOLD decision

step 6 → send the proposed trade through the risk management team, where aggressive, neutral and conservative perspectives evaluate the downside before portfolio approval

step 7 → collect the final decisions, plot the signals on an ETH chart and compare them against historical price movements to evaluate the strategy

step 8 → backtest the decisions across multiple market conditions with realistic fees and slippage before even considering real capital

the result: an open-source multi-agent trading research system where AI analysts debate market opportunities, challenge risk and produce structured trading decisions

the framework is free, although AI API usage may cost money, and the terminal in the clip is a visual demonstration rather than live executed trades

i won't say anything more...

excluded_hits.draft_en:
Claude, Obsidian and loop engineering together give you a vault that maintains itself.

Main idea: the loop's state lives in the vault, not in the chat window.

Anything Claude Code needs to remember sits in a .md file. It's the Karpathy-style second brain, now set up to run on its own.

How the loop goes:
- capture: a new thought lands in 00-inbox
- context: Opus 5.5 gathers links, tags and related notes
- draft: Sonnet 5.5 does the editing in its own git worktree, the live vault stays untouched
- review: Haiku 5.5 plays critic and reads the diff before anything goes out
- commit: added to the vault, nothing overwritten

What matters most: frontmatter fields such as supports, contradicts and supersedes work as graph edges, not just metadata.

The note format doubles as the write API, and the second brain keeps compounding on that base.

Begin with a simple loop. It runs at roughly 2-4x a direct call.
Only upgrade to a full graph if:
- state needs to survive past the session
- multiple agents have to coordinate
- you have to be able to explain what changed
That step up can run 10-50x.

Case in point: a review assistant climbed 55% -> 72% -> 84% simply by stepping through these shapes one at a time.
